chapters.title: A Table That Does Not Fit

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The Guild Hall of Steady Steps has a problem, and the problem is a table.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: It is a very good table. I built it myself. It seats sixty. The hall seats forty. I measured twice, then I measured the hall, and then I sat down.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: It is a magnificent table, Maple! The only thing wrong with it is the hall.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I have been counting. We have more members than chairs, and more chairs than socks. I do not know how that happened.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Someone small and brisk is standing in the doorway, in a maroon cardigan and a beret, holding a notebook and wearing the look of a person who has just been handed a present.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: Good afternoon! Is this the place one begins? I am eighty-three and I would very much like to begin.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Eighty-three! A fine age to begin! I started at Level 2!

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: He did not.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I have made a list. Item one: stretch. Item two: ask someone what stretching is. Item three: tea.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I'll show you the Duck Mat, Bertram. Everyone starts on the Duck Mat.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Someone told me once that the wall counts. So I'll tell you too: the wall counts.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Someone told me once to rest at every landing. I'll show you where all of ours are.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Someone once walked right beside me, so I will walk right beside you. That is how it is done here.

nodes.prompt: What do you say to Bertram?

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: Am I? I was sure I was either too early or about forty years late. Exactly on time. I shall write it down.

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: Wherever I like! Oh, that is a thrilling thing to be told. I like the kettle. Let us begin with the kettle.

options.label: Tea first, and then everything else.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: That is the correct order. I wrote it on a sign. The sign is also in the kitchen.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The table has been carried out into the courtyard in nine pieces and put together again in the sunshine. It stretches nearly from one wall to the other, and it is still not quite long enough.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: What if the table is not the problem? What if we simply have never invited enough people to need it?

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: That is not a solution, Chad. That is the problem again, wearing a hat.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: A feast! A long table, for everyone who ever came through our door. The coast, the mountain, the valley. Everyone!

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Fennel could carry the invitations. Fennel is very good at roads now, and at stopping.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I shall write them! I have excellent handwriting and no commitments until Thursday.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Nothing here has a deadline. People will come when they come, and the table will wait.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: And anyone who cannot come, we will save a chair for. Rest is training, after all. A chair is just a rest with legs.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Biscuit, who has been listening carefully to the word 'feast', sits down very close to the table and does not move for the rest of the afternoon.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: Forty-one letters, four roads, and I am walking. On purpose! I have stopped for tea twice already.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I have written every one by hand. The first twenty say 'Dear Friend'. The last twenty-one say 'Dear Friend' with a doodle. I got bored of the first version.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: What does the invitation say, exactly? I would like to hear it. I have not been shown it. I am the host.

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: 'Come as you are.' I shall add 'in whatever shoes you have.' Shoes are important at my age.

options.label: Bring a chair, or do not.

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: 'Bring a chair, or do not.' Perfect. It tells them everything they need and nothing they do not.

reply.speaker: fennel
reply.text: 'There is soup.' That has worked on me every time. I have been trapped in a hut by it for a week.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: People don't always know they're allowed to come to things. It helps to be told, in writing, with a doodle.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: They walk on towards the sea, and the doodles on the letters grow bolder with every mile.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: A feast! For everyone! Oh, I would love that. Gullhaven is very good at shifts now. The lamp is looked after by a rota of eleven people and a dog.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: I still have the spark you struck. I keep it in a jar. It is quite well-behaved.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: Everybody helped you light it. It is the only way I would light it now. Together, and not tidily.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: Pip lights the great lamp every Friday now. They have become excellent at it. They still ask if they can.

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: I shall set off today. I will arrive when I arrive.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: Excellent! Item: ferry. May I ask how long a tortoise's 'today' is?

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: About three weeks.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: He has never missed a party, and he has never once been on time. Those are very different things.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: That is the thing I was getting wrong for two winters, you know. You can arrive without being early.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Sedge adjusts his small red cap, lowers himself gently into the water, and begins the longest journey in the whole of the story, at exactly the speed he likes.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The road up to the snow line is much shorter than it used to be, now that everyone in the party knows where all the landings are. They arrive at the little stone hut in good time and in a good mood.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: You are back. I put a mug on the step. I always do. This time somebody picked it up.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: Is this a hut? It is exactly the size of a hut. I do so admire a building that knows what it is.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: I carried a pot all the way here. It was empty, and I still have strong opinions about it.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: Hush, we are having a feast. For everyone. There is a table with sixty seats, and it needs soup.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: Soup for sixty. ...I can do soup for forty. I would need a bigger pot for sixty.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: I have a bigger pot. I did not know why I brought it. Now I know.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: On a mountain every path has a hut. In a hall, every table needs a kitchen. It is the same rule with different shoes.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I will give a speech about soup. It is a very moving speech. It has a goose in it.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: Sit down, Chad.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: ...Sitting down.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: Mr Hush, may I help? I cannot lift anything heavy, but I can stir for as long as anyone likes. I have wonderful patience and an unreasonable number of spoons.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: You may stir. If you stir, someone else rests. That is how a kitchen is kept warm.

nodes.prompt: What do you bring to the table?

reply.speaker: hush
reply.text: A lopsided pie tastes best. It has been loved too hard to sit up straight.

options.label: My own soup, for Hush to try.

reply.speaker: hush
reply.text: Oh. Nobody has ever brought me soup. ...It is very good. I will need to sit down.

options.label: A very large bag of apples.

reply.speaker: brad
reply.text: Apples! I will carry them. I have been looking for a purpose all day and this is a good one.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: Rest is training. I have been resting since the bell rang and look at me! I am nearly exactly as good as I was.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: By evening the hut is steaming at every window, and the biggest pot in the mountains is gently bubbling in front of the stove, with Bertram standing guard over it with a very long spoon.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The old wood is as green and as slow as ever. A great many tiny, patient saplings have sprung up around Oakhelm's roots, and not one of them is in a hurry either.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Oakhelm, we need chairs. A great many chairs. For a feast. We would be so grateful for a few branches.

nodes.speaker: oakhelm
nodes.text: ...Chairs. ...I have... been thinking... about chairs... since... Tuesday.

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: BUTTONS! For the cushions! I have eleven hundred. They are all different. It is the best day of my life.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: Mr Oakhelm, I should say that I am eighty-three, and I have never been so thoroughly understood by a tree.

nodes.speaker: oakhelm
nodes.text: ...We... are... the same... speed... you and I.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: It takes the whole afternoon, and very few of the branches come down. The wood decides, gently, which ones are ready. Nobody asks it to hurry. Nobody could.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Sixty-three chairs. None match. I have never been so happy.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: And a special one for me! The host! Which chair shall I have, {hero}? You choose. I trust you with my posterior.

nodes.prompt: What kind of chair should Chad get?

options.label: One with a very tall back.

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: A tall back! Like a throne! Maple, I am going to need a longer cape.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: You do not have a cape. You have a towel.

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: A rocking chair! I shall sway all through the speeches. Nobody will know whether I am nervous or just enjoying myself.

options.label: One with a cushion shaped like a duck.

reply.speaker: grit
reply.text: I can do a duck! I have buttons for the eyes! They are different sizes! That is what makes it a good duck!

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: I have never been so honoured in my life.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I have added chairs to my list, Mr Chad. Item forty-seven. Item forty-eight is a cushion for the dog.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Every chair here is different, and every one of them fits someone. That is the whole trick, I think.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Where the road runs out, the sand begins. It is warm and gold and very quiet, apart from the sound of something very large thinking.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: I have one letter left for the desert. It says 'Dear Friend', and then a drawing of a table, and then a drawing of a very long table.

nodes.speaker: sphinx
nodes.text: Welcome. I will ask you a riddle. If you answer, I shall come to your feast. If you do not, I shall come to your feast anyway. But I do enjoy asking.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: How marvellous. I have always wanted to be asked a riddle by a cat. A very large cat. A cat of enormous dignity.

nodes.speaker: sphinx
nodes.text: What can be had by anyone, costs nothing, makes everything better, and is best taken at your own pace?

reply.speaker: sphinx
reply.text: ...Correct. It is always correct. Nobody has ever got it wrong, you know. I just like to ask.

reply.speaker: sphinx
reply.text: Soup! ...Well, that is also true. I shall allow it. Soup has been described as a kind of nap.

options.label: I would rather you told me.

reply.speaker: sphinx
reply.text: That is the wisest answer I have ever been given. The answer is a nap. Please tell no one.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The sand ahead rises into a hill, and the hill, very slowly, turns round and looks at them.

nodes.speaker: worm
nodes.text: HELLO.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: Hello! Is he always like this?

nodes.speaker: sphinx
nodes.text: He says hello with his whole body. It is a gift. It is also a lot.

nodes.speaker: worm
nodes.text: I... AM... COMING... TO... THE... TABLE... DO... I... FIT?

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: We will make you a seat, and it will fit. A very long seat. Probably the table's whole second half.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: Item sixty-one: make sure the table is longer than the worm.

nodes.speaker: worm
nodes.text: THANK... YOU. ...I... HAVE... NEVER... BEEN... INVITED... TO... ANYTHING.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: That is exactly the sort of thing the letters are for. Nobody ever stops being glad to be asked.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The whole way back across the dunes, the Dune Worm comes up beside them every few minutes to say hello again, just in case it did not land the first time.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: At the foot of the long stair, somebody in a storm-blue coat is sitting on a folding chair with a thermos, looking at the steps she has just come down.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: I said I would come down by stages, and I did. Eleven days. Forty-one landings. I sat at every one.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: You sat beside me at the bottom of my stair once. I thought of that at every landing on the way down.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: You asked me to try one step. It turned out to be a great many steps, taken one at a time. That is the trick.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: You asked me about the view. I have now seen it from the top and from every landing. They are all different.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: Eleven days for four hundred and twelve steps! That is thirty-seven steps a day! I shall put that in my notebook as the finest piece of arithmetic I have ever heard.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: It is not about the arithmetic. It was about the landings. At every one, I thought: this is a place a person can stop.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: A place a person can stop. I might put that on a banner.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: You are coming to the feast, then?

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: I would not miss it. And I have brought someone. He insisted. He has also brought a weather forecast.

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: Hello! I came down the stair on my own. Mostly. Tamsin was at the other end the whole time, which counts for a good deal.

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: Tamsin led and I followed, and it came out right. I still think about that note.

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: You let me ring first, once. I think about that more than the weather, and the weather is my whole job.

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: We rang it all together, the three of us and the whole mountain. I think that is how it will always be.

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: I have been asked for a forecast for the feast. It is my first official forecast. I am a little bit nervous, which, as you know, shows up in the sky.

nodes.prompt: What weather should Skarn send for the feast?

reply.speaker: skarn
reply.text: A clear night. Stars, and no wind. I can do that. I have been practising. I will only be slightly damp in the top corner.

reply.speaker: skarn
reply.text: A breeze, just enough to make the lanterns sway. Yes! I can make a breeze. I have a lot of sighs in reserve.

reply.speaker: tamsin
reply.text: That is the bravest forecast anyone has asked for. I think we will all be a little rained on and glad of it.

reply.speaker: skarn
reply.text: Oh. Oh, I think I might cry. That is a weather. I am sorry.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: Item seventy-three: umbrellas, and also not umbrellas.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: By dusk the courtyard looks like the inside of a kind person's head. Lanterns hang in strings from wall to wall, sixty-three mismatched chairs line a table that is finally long enough, and there is a smell of soup from every direction.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: I have counted the chairs eleven times. There is one for everyone. There is one for the worm, and it is a long one. There is one for a person I have not met yet, in case.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: In case! The best two words in the language! Maple, I do not tell you often enough that you are the backbone of this guild.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: You tell me every Tuesday. It is on a banner. I am keeping the banner.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I used to think a guild was a place where people who know what they are doing teach people who do not. Now I think it is just a place with enough chairs.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I have crossed off every single item on my list, except the last. 'Be here when it happens.' I do not think one crosses that off. One simply keeps doing it.

nodes.prompt: What would you like to give the guild?

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: A story! The guild runs on them. I will tell it at the tavern, slightly improved, with you as a considerably more handsome hero.

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: A song! I shall learn the words. It may take me until Thursday. I am an excellent slow learner.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: An afternoon. ...That is the most valuable thing I have ever been offered. I will put it in the pantry for later.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: One by one, in the lantern light, the guests are arriving. They come along the road from the coast, down the pass, through the dunes and up from the fog, and every one of them stops at the gate to look at the table and breathe out.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: I brought the pot. It is the biggest in the mountains. It needed seven people to lift it, and four of them were soup.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: The lamp is lit and Gullhaven is minding it. I have not been away from it for a night in forty-one years. I do not think I have ever felt so rested.

nodes.speaker: murmur
nodes.text: I did not think I would come. I thought: what if I arrive and nobody remembers me? ...And then somebody said my name before I had even got to the gate.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: Nothing here has a deadline, Murmur. That includes arriving. You were exactly on time.

nodes.speaker: skarn
nodes.text: It is going to be a clear night with a breeze. It is working. I can feel it working. Nobody look at me.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The feast begins with a sound that is very hard to describe: forty people, a tortoise, a worm and a dog all sitting down at once and discovering that they all fit.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Friends! Guild! Strangers who are about to stop being strangers! I will keep this brief. I have prepared a speech with a goose in it. I am not going to give it.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I started this guild with a hall, a bell, and a dog. Everything else is you. Every chair at this table is somebody who walked in, and somebody who walked in after them.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: Hear, hear. And to the people who rested, and the people who stopped, and the people who came back. Those are the ones who made the hall.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: I made soup. That was my part. I would like it to be enough.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: It is enough. It is always enough. That is what soup is for.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I would like to say that eighty-three is a fine age to begin. Also eighty-four. I plan to try that one as well.

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: Between us! The best seat! You will hear everything twice, once from each side, and a third time at the end of the evening.

reply.speaker: tamsin
reply.text: Then you will be sitting beside half the table. It is a good place to be.

options.label: At the end, where I can see everyone.

reply.speaker: wren
reply.text: The end of a table is a lighthouse. You can see everyone, and everyone can see you. I recommend it.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The lanterns sway in a small, careful breeze. Overhead the stars are bright and orderly, and only one of them, near the top corner, is very slightly damp.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Every chair is full. There is a chair left over, at the far end, and I have decided it is for whoever arrives next.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I think that is the point of it. Whoever comes next, there is always one more seat.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I have a last item for my list. Item one hundred and four: thank you. I do not think I need to cross it off.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Biscuit has gone to sleep under the table, with a sausage. I would like it noted that this is exactly where he is supposed to be.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Move however you like, rest when you need to, and always bring a chair. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Have fun with it, the way you said you would, and bring a friend, or a worm. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Stay curious, the way you did from the very first day. There is a seat for whatever you find. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Far away a bell rings, and a lamp winks, and a chime sings across the dark. Under all of it, a very long table, laid for everyone, at their own pace, with one chair kept for whoever comes next.
